record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.original_question: For an n x n positive semidefinite matrix A=(a_ij) and real alpha, define det_alpha(A) as the sum over permutations sigma in S_n of alpha raised to n minus the number of cycles of sigma, multiplied by the product over i=1,...,n of a_{i,sigma(i)}. If 0 <= alpha <= 2, must det_alpha(A) be nonnegative?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ positive semidefinite (Hermitian) matrix and let $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$. Define the $\alpha$-determinant of $A$ by
$$\det{}_{\alpha}(A)\;=\;\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\alpha^{\,n-\nu(\sigma)}\prod_{i=1}^{n}a_{i,\sigma(i)},$$
where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $n$ letters and $\nu(\sigma)$ denotes the number of cycles of $\sigma$ (including fixed points). Note that $\det_{-1}(A)=\det(A)$ and $\det_{1}(A)=\operatorname{per}(A)$.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n\ge 1$, every $n\times n$ positive semidefinite matrix $A$, and every real number $\alpha$ with $0\le\alpha\le 2$,
$$\det{}_{\alpha}(A)\;\ge\;0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The positivity problem for the alpha-determinant was raised by Shirai and Takahashi and studied by Vere-Jones and others. Positivity is known for special values such as α = 1 (the permanent of a PSD matrix, Schur) and α a nonnegative integer multiple of 1/2 via Wishart-type identities, and for α in a neighborhood of 0 (Shirai). The full claim that det_α(A) ≥ 0 for all PSD A whenever 0 ≤ α ≤ 2 remains a conjecture in general; it is established only in restricted parameter ranges or low dimensions, while α > 2 is known to fail.

status_evidence.title: Remarks on the positivity of α-determinants
status_evidence.snippet: Positivity problem for α-determinants; α ≤ 2 is necessary for positivity in the real symmetric case.
status_evidence.claim: The 0 ≤ α ≤ 2 boundary is identified, with partial results establishing positivity only in subranges.

status_evidence.title: Remarks on the α-permanent
status_evidence.snippet: Studies α-permanent positivity, related to Vere-Jones' permanent and Shirai-Takahashi's α-determinant.
status_evidence.claim: Question of full positivity on [0,2] remains active and not fully settled.
